trust_decision.summary: The reader decides which header a pending PAX 'size' record applies to (and so where the next header starts). At the pinned commit, next_entry_raw applies it to whatever header comes next, including intermediary GNU L/K and PAX x/g extension headers.

landing_point.why: This is the only place that reads PAX_SIZE and overrides the header size. A 'PAX header desync' summary leads straight to it.

fix_sites.entry_point: Archive::entries / Archive::entries_with_seek / Archive::unpack (all through EntriesFields::next_entry -> next_entry_raw)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 parser differentials: 'duplicate or malformed PAX records are a separate malformed-input issue, not the extension-header ordering the report describes'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The PAX size (and path/linkpath/uid/gid) must still apply to the real file entry after an intervening GNU L/K header: x -> L -> file must give the file the PAX size and the L long name. Clearing pending PAX state at an L header, or ignoring PAX size for GNU sparse entries, breaks legitimate archives (sizes over the octal limit, long names).

O6_input_shapes: PAX x followed by GNU LongName L
PAX x followed by GNU LongLink K
PAX x followed by PAX global g
PAX x followed by a further x (also already rejected at src/archive.rs:435-441)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate 'size' records in one PAX header: pax_extensions_value returns the first match, while common tar implementations use the last one, so the parsers disagree on the entry boundary.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Duplicate keys are malformed input and the report is about which header the record applies to.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A malformed record before 'size', or a non-numeric size value, makes pax_extensions_value return None, so the code silently falls back to the ustar header size instead of failing.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Graceful fallback on bad PAX data looks like intended leniency.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The published fix classifies extension headers by entry type alone, but next_entry consumes L/K/x only when the header has GNU/ustar magic, so a v7-magic 'L' after 'x' is returned as a regular entry yet no longer gets the PAX size.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Headers without magic are legacy or unsupported, and the type-only check matches the upstream astral-tokio-tar fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Apply PAX uid/gid (or a newly honoured key such as mtime) to the header in the same block, so it still leaks onto extension headers if a solver gates only size.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The block already overrides uid/gid in place, and a maintainer adding mtime or other keys here would follow the same pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PAX GNU.sparse.realsize/size override used in sparse handling, which advances self.next independently.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pax.rs already defines the GNU.sparse.* keys (src/pax.rs:27-36) without using them, so wiring them into parse_sparse_header is a natural feature addition.

O9_family: Parser differential / archive entry-boundary desynchronisation (CWE-20, CWE-843)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo (stable); dev-deps include tokio and astral-tokio-tar 0.6 for cross-checking
O10_build.project_tests: tests/all.rs (pax_size_smuggled_symlink at tests/all.rs:2019, pax_size_smuggle_matches_astral_tokio_tar at tests/all.rs:2049) with fixtures in tests/archives/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Skip PAX size only when the next header is a GNU long name, and leave K, g and the duplicate-key or malformed-record behaviour in src/pax.rs alone.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit message cites GHSA-3cv2-h65g-fgmm (astral-tokio-tar). The advisory ID given here is GHSA-3PV8-6F4R-FFG2; treat them as one issue mirrored across both crates.
An earlier PAX size smuggling fix already exists at the pinned commit (tests/all.rs:2019-2050), which is the sibling advisory.
unverified: Whether the O8 differentials (first-wins duplicate size, silent fallback on a malformed record, magic-less L) are treated as vulnerabilities by the maintainers or by astral-tokio-tar; there was no network access to compare.
Whether GNU tar, Go and other reference parsers use last-wins for duplicate PAX keys; this comes from general knowledge, not from code in this repository.
Repo size in MB was not measured. The source is 9 small files under src/, so tiny_repo (<5 MB) very likely holds, but the size was not confirmed.
present_in_latest is unknown for every O8 route because no latest release was provided.
That 'single_site' is a red flag holds only if the O8 differentials are judged out of scope; the fix itself changes one function at one place.
